title: Simple Versus Radical Hysterectomy for Stage I Cervical Cancer
brief_summary: The primary objective of this study is to assess the preferences (values and utilities) of women for complications and recurrences associated with the surgical treatment of cervical cancer. A secondary objective of this study is to compare the preferences of women at high-risk for developing cervix cancer with the preferences of women who have already been diagnosed with cervix cancer.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Women who are at least 18 years of age.
2. Women who speak English
3. Women presenting to the Colposcopy Clinic in the Gynecologic Oncology Clinic at M.D. Anderson Cancer Center OR women with an established diagnosis of either Stage IA2 or IB1 cervix cancer treated with radical hysterectomy 3-24 months prior to presenting to the Gynecologic Oncology

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Women who are not 18 years of age.
2. Women who are non-English speakers.
3. Women with a diagnosis of any type of cancer other than cervical cancer.
4. Women who are currently pregnant.
study_population: Participants at high-risk for cervical cancer and those already diagnosed with cervical cancer.
